videos.title: Gemini Skills for repeatable tasks
summary: Futurepedia highlights Google Gemini's "Skills" feature, framing it as a way to turn a one-off conversation into a reusable, packaged workflow instead of starting from scratch each time.

The video gives two concrete entry points: grabbing a ready-made prompt from a free skills guide to spin up a first skill in a new chat, or revisiting a past chat where the user already iterated with Gemini to get something right and asking it to bundle that exchange into a skill.

The pitch is that most of the work users think they still need to do manually has already happened in earlier chats, and the video positions Skills as the mechanism for capturing that prior iteration so repeatable tasks (reports, templated replies, recurring formats) stop requiring re-prompting from zero.

videos.title: How the Top 1% Use Claude Code Differently
summary: Simon Scrapes argues that expert usage patterns for Claude Code have shifted significantly over the past year, and that older advice — relying on "plan mode," prompting it to "think harder," and other once-common conventions — is now largely obsolete.

The video walks through ten updated strategies top users apply instead, including treating plan mode as redundant, skipping manual effort-level selection, distinguishing "checks" from "plans," defaulting to autonomous runs via a /goal-style command, turning CLAUDE.md into an index rather than a monolithic doc, writing custom Skills only for what Claude gets wrong, favoring no-Skill approaches most of the time, encoding must-hold rules in hooks, and letting Claude assemble its own sub-agent team.

Framed around building more autonomous, less supervised Claude Code workflows, the video functions as an advanced-practices update for viewers already using Claude Code who want to modernize their setup past six-month-old conventions.

videos.title: 10 ChatGPT Broken Codes
summary: Sabrina Ramonov shares 10 short prompt "codes" meant to replace ChatGPT's often vague default answers with sharper, more targeted responses by prefacing a question with one of the codes.

The codes include LINDYMODE, 80/20, TRUTHMODE, ELI10, REDTEAM, HORMOZI, YCOMBINATOR, GARYVEE, SOCRATES, and FUTUREYOU, each nudging the model toward a different response style — for example ELI10 for a simplified explanation, 80/20 for the highest-value points only, and SOCRATES for a question-driven, teaching-style answer.
The format mirrors the channel's earlier prompt-code videos, positioning this as a quick-reference list viewers can paste in front of any ChatGPT question to get more specific, less generic output.

videos.title: Claude + Canva Is a Literal Cheat Code
summary: Sabrina Ramonov demonstrates connecting Canva to Claude via Claude's Connectors settings, enabling Claude to generate Canva-based designs directly from a chat.

She walks through the setup (Settings → Connectors → Browse Connectors → Add Canva) and shows asking Claude to produce graphics, posters, Instagram carousels, and branded content using the user's existing Canva templates, brand kit, and colors, with the option to have Claude post the results to social media from within the chat.

The video targets creators and small-business owners who build their own marketing visuals, pitching the Claude-Canva connector as a way to design social content without switching between separate apps and tabs.
